input.quote: (i) From time to time, the Class A Certificateholder may, solely at its option, deposit amounts into the Acquisition Account, as set forth in Section 2.5 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume restriction is imposed on our side. The only recurring "purchase" mechanic is the acquisition of Additional Receivables in Article II, and it is entirely discretionary and condition-based: funding of the Acquisition Account is made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option" (p0223), and each transfer is "[s]ubject to the satisfaction of the conditions in Section 2.1(d)" — a Transfer Notice plus satisfaction of the Credit Enhancement Test and Pool Composition Tests (p0037, p0039). The Issuer pays only the Additional Receivables Cash Transfer Amount actually withdrawn from the Acquisition Account for receivables it acquires (p0224), excess amounts are released to Certificateholders (p0225), and the account is swept on entry into the Amortization Period (p0226), which operates as the exit. The Required Acquisition Deposit and Required Negative Carry Amount are structural funding mechanics tied to amounts the Certificateholder chose to deposit, not a shortfall penalty. The only "shortfall" obligation found (p0211) runs against the Marketing Agent in our favour. This meets the preferred position (fees/consideration for assets actually acquired, no committed volume), so no redline.
